title: Per-credential credit overhang causing silent throttles and billing miscounts
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Short summary: Observed intermittent customer reports of unexplained throttles while usage dashboards show available quota. Root cause appears to be a 'credit overhang' where reclaimed credits from completed requests are not immediately reflected in per-credential ledgers, causing the enforcer to decide incorrectly to throttle new requests even though the tenant has capacity. This affects per-key and per-org scopes, manifests more on routes with cross-tenant burst patterns, and leads to both customer-visible latency and underreported usage totals.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a synthetic workload that alternates heavy bursts from two API keys targeting the same route with different priorities.
Simulate high ingestion rate with short-lived requests to trigger rapid credit reclaim paths.
Introduce a reconciliation worker delay (simulated by adding 1500ms sleep) to reproduce credit not propagated to in-memory enforcer.
Observe that requests get 429s while billing dashboard shows available credits for the org.
investigation_log: 2026-02-12: First customer report (Cust A) — intermittent 429s during sustained low-latency bursts; initial triage by SRE suggested enforcer overload.
2026-02-18: Added diagnostics to enforcer: per-key ledger snapshots, last-reclaimed timestamps, and reconciliation queue depth.
2026-02-24: Correlation found between high reconciliation queue depth and throttle spikes; suspect GC/concurrent-reclaim race.
2026-03-02: Reproduced locally by injecting delay into credit-reclaim path; confirmed ledger state lag of 800-2200ms where reclaimed credit persisted only in DB but not in in-memory enforcer.

2026-03-07: Observed secondary effect: usage accounting undercounts because reclaimed credits are not atomically reconciled with billed tokens, causing billing dashboards to show lower consumption than actual.
root_cause: The credit-reclaim path and the in-memory enforcer ledger are updated asynchronously with a non-atomic handoff. Under bursty conditions, reclaimed credits are written to the persistent store and queued for reconciliation but the in-memory enforcer uses stale ledger snapshots until the reconciliation worker processes the queue. A race when GC reduces ledger entries triggers a window where the enforcer believes credits are exhausted. Additionally, the reconciliation job batches updates and can drop low-priority reconciliation items under load, amplifying the overhang.
proposed_fix: Make the reclaim-to-enforcer update atomic: emit an in-process event before persisting that immediately updates the in-memory ledger, with a compensating reconciliation for persistent store consistency.
Add backpressure and bounded queueing to the reconciliation worker to avoid silent drop of low-priority items.
Introduce a fast-path for recently reclaimed credits: keep a time-bounded cache of reclaimed deltas consulted by the enforcer until reconciliation completes.
Add metrics and traces: 'credit_overhang_ms', 'reconciliation_queue_drop_count', and per-credential 'last_reclaim_ts'.
rollout_plan: Implement fix in rate-engine branch with feature flag 'fast_reclaim' toggled off by default.
Unit and integration tests for race scenarios and high-burst synthetic workload.
Deploy Canary to staging and then to a small subset of hosts (Dedicated customers + internal apis) for 48h monitoring.
If stable, gradual rollout over 2 days with monitoring and automatic rollback on threshold breaches (error rate > 1% or 'credit_overhang_ms' > 1000ms).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: In-process event could briefly double-count credits if reconciliation retry occurs. Mitigation: use idempotent deltas and versioned ledger updates.
Risk: Backpressure may increase latency under extreme load. Mitigation: tune queue bounds and add graceful shedding with informative 429 reason codes.
Risk: Metrics cardinality growth from per-credential traces. Mitigation: sample low-volume keys and aggregate.
postmortem_followups: Audit other enforcers (per-route, global) for similar async handoffs.
Add e2e billing tests that validate reconciliation under burst workloads.
Document failure modes and update runbooks for SRE and support with diagnostic queries and dashboards.
